title: Bidding Policy
description: Buyer-authored execution policy for auction bidding, average outcome cost, or return on ad spend. The containing object determines authored scope: media-buy `bidding` is a complete inherited default and package `bidding` is a complete package override. Sellers MUST preserve authored scope on readback and MUST NOT copy an inherited media-buy policy into package `bidding`. Currency is the media-buy currency and is not repeated here. A media-buy policy is valid only when every inheriting package resolves compatible units for each supplied field. Absence means seller/provider automatic delivery; it does not mean a zero bid. Sellers MUST reject unsupported modes, combinations, units, or native placements before any provider mutation and MUST NOT silently convert between bid amount, auction ceiling, cost cap/target, or ROAS floor/target semantics.

bid_amount.description: Manual auction bid in the selected pricing option's auction unit. This is the amount submitted to the auction, not a promise that the clearing price equals this amount. Requires an auction-priced pricing option.

max_bid.description: Hard per-auction ceiling in the selected pricing option's auction unit. This is the only canonical hard auction ceiling and MUST NOT be translated into an average outcome-cost control. Requires an auction-priced pricing option. May stand alone or supplement cost_per/roas only when the provider supports that combination.

cost_per.description: Average cost control per result of the package's primary optimization goal. The primary goal is priority 1, otherwise the lowest numeric priority, otherwise the first array entry.

amount.description: Average cost amount per primary-goal result in the media-buy currency.

strength.description: `cap` optimizes for an average at or below the amount and accepts underdelivery when necessary; `target` optimizes around the amount while balancing volume and spend. Neither is a per-result or per-auction guarantee.

roas.description: Dimensionless return-on-ad-spend control. Requires value-bearing event sources on every package to which the policy applies.

value.description: Return per unit of ad spend; 4 means 4 units of value per 1 unit spent.

strength.description: `floor` prefers underdelivery to knowingly optimizing below the requested return; `target` optimizes around the requested return. Neither guarantees realized return.
